newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding temporary reserves.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding temporary reserves.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Friday, analysts said.
Daiwa Securities America Inc. expects the Fed to add reserves through $2.0 billion in customer repurchases.
James Glassman said the Fed could add reserves through six-day system repurchases.

"There's a small add need," he said. "They weren't too aggressive with the nine-day system repurchases (on Monday) so they have $2.0 to $3.0 billion to do. I think some sort of operation today is likely.
Analysts at MMS International expect the Fed to intervene "with at least a customer repurchase today."
At BZT Securities, senior economist Waldo Best said he expected the Fed to refrain from action.
Shortly before the Fed's usual operation time, Fed funds were trading at 5-1/4 percent, the Fed's target for the rate.
